title: Rocket Launch
strapline: Count down from ten, fire the boosters, and blast off to a planet the children have invented.
intent: Children count down from ten with real anticipation, meeting number in its most thrilling form.
Children build and rebuild a rocket, planning it, testing it and adapting when it doesn't work.
Children stretch their imaginations to somewhere no one has been — space, other planets, the far side of the moon.
Children take on roles — pilot, ground control, astronaut — and cooperate to run the mission.
Children ask big questions about space, the stars and how things move, and expect real answers.
implementation: Make a big countdown a daily event — ten, nine, eight... BLAST OFF! — so number becomes a shared drumroll.
Provide crates, boxes and tubes for building a rocket children can climb inside, and let them redesign it.
Offer a control panel of dials and buttons and headphones for ground control to talk to the crew.
Feed in space vocabulary — orbit, gravity, astronaut, planet, launch — and use it as you play.
Set genuine challenges: how will the astronauts eat? What will they find on the new planet?
Add a dark den with fairy-light stars for a moonwalk in slow motion.
Follow children's real questions about the moon and stars, looking things up together.
key_questions: Shall we count down together — ready, from ten?
How could we make the rocket strong enough to hold the whole crew?
What do you think you'll find when you land on the new planet?
How will the astronauts eat and sleep so far from home?
Why do things float in space — what do you think?

impact.text: Children count down from ten with growing accuracy and huge anticipation.
Children design, build and rebuild a rocket, adapting the plan when it doesn't work.
Children invent rich imaginative missions with roles, story and rules, and keep them going.
Children take up new space vocabulary from stories and topic talk and use it in play.
Children ask real questions about space and make predictions about what they'll find.
Children persist with a wobbly rocket build until it holds together and feel the win.

enhancements: Big crates, boxes and tubes for a climb-in rocket the children design.
A control panel of dials, buttons, switches and a big red launch button.
Headphones and walkie-talkies linking ground control to the crew.
A dark den with fairy-light stars and a moon to walk on.
Space suits, helmets (colanders) and moon boots for the crew.
Foil-wrapped 'space food' pouches and a menu for the long journey.
A number-line countdown strip and a big 10-to-0 launch chart.

playing_exploring: Children imagine the impossible and throw everything into the mission.
They test their rocket design by climbing in and seeing if it holds.
active_learning: Children rebuild the rocket again and again until it's strong enough.
The countdown gives the play a shared goal everyone drives towards.
creating_thinking: Children plan the build, invent the planet, and solve how astronauts live in space.
They make links between what they've heard about space and what they build.
